newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco sees 150 mln tonne Voisey's resource.
newsitem.headline: Inco sees 150 mln tonne Voisey's resource.

text.p: Inco Ltd said Monday that indicated mineral resources at its rich Voisey's Bay nickel property in remote Labrador measure about 150 million tonnes.

New resource calculations for the Eastern Deeps deposit on the property show an indicated resource of 50 million tonnes containing 1.36 percent nickel, 0.67 percent copper and 0.09 percent cobalt, the company said in a statement.
Inco also said nickel mineralization has been intersected in drilling over a distance of one km east of the Eastern Deeps.
The company has also exposed several geophysical anomalies that indicate the possible presence of significant resources both to the east of Eastern Deeps and two km to the south.
Inco said it is still drilling to define a new zone of high grade mineralization in the Western Extension part of the Voisey's Bay site.
A third zone, the Ovoid, has already been defined to show reserves of 31.7 million tonnes of ore containing 2.83 percent nickel, 1.68 percent coper and 0.12 percent cobalt.
The nickel giant's third quarter earnings fell, however.
Inco blamed lower metal prices for third quarter earnings of US$29 million or US$0.19 a share, down from US$44 million or US$0.33 cents a share a year earlier.
Inco's average realized nickel price in the third quarter was US$3.50 a pound, down from US$3.92 a pound in the third quarter of last year.
The company's average copper price was US$1.07 per pound in the third quarter of 1996, compared to US$1.24 a year earlier.
Inco said operations were hurt by an explosion at one of the company's three furnaces in Indonesia and a two-week strike in Thompson, Manitoba this autumn.
Total deliveries of nickel fell in the quarter from 130,000 pounds in 1996 compared to 145,000 in 1995, but deliveries of company produced nickel increased, Inco said.
Inco supplies its clients with both company-produced nickel and nickel bought on the world market.
Nickel inventories were 59 million pounds at the end of September, down from 67 million pounds at the end of June 1996.
